audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Nasus wins 54.03% but the chart gives Jax 5/7 stages vs 1.' The real error is not the chart — it is diff HARD / difficulty 7/10 on a matchup Nasus wins over 720 games.
audit.why: Jax genuinely does own levels 2 through first item; that is what every line of the entry describes and it is why the chart reads the way it does. Rewriting a stage to Nasus to balance the chart would invent a power shift and get someone killed at level 4. The honest resolution is that the lane is hard and the matchup is not: the win rate comes from Nasus outscaling, which is exactly what the 2+ items stage already says.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 6/10, breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line aligned. The stage chart is left alone deliberately.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described only as dodging 'your Q auto' and 'autos', with nothing said about what it does not dodge.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks. Spirit Fire is a ground-placed ability and Fury of the Sands is an aura — neither is a basic attack, so both keep applying through his E. That converts the E window from 'do nothing for two seconds' into 'hold Siphoning Strike, keep the zone on him, take the free chip'. For a champion whose entire trade is one empowered auto, knowing which of his tools still work during the enemy's defensive window is the single most useful thing in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, the Level 3 stage, dontsFull and the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns said 'Dodges autos + stuns. Wither him after' with no duration, and the entry never gives a number for the one cooldown it tells the player to track.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9. Seventeen seconds at rank 1 is an enormous window and it shrinks by nearly half as he maxes it — that shape is why the early lane is survivable and the mid lane is not. 'Track it' without the number is not trackable.
audit.corrected: 17s at rank 1 stated in breakdown.cooldowns, Level 3 stage, early text, whys[2] and spikes[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Jax's attack speed to 'his Empower attack speed' and calls his kit 'attack-speed-reliant' without naming the source.
audit.why: Empower is a flat bonus-damage auto reset; it grants no attack speed. The stacking attack speed is Relentless Assault, his passive, built from consecutive basic attacks. That matters because Wither's attack-speed component is what dismantles it, and because Grandmaster-at-Arms' every-third-attack magic damage is also gated on him landing consecutive swings — Wither delays both from one cast.
audit.corrected: Relentless Assault and Grandmaster-at-Arms named in mid, late, whys[4], whys[6] and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4] 'Level 6' says 'the first real fight you're allowed to take' and its own content layer says 'ult only to survive a committed dive, not to chase a kill'. content win[4] gives the stage to Jax.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms gives Jax bonus armour and magic resist on demand plus a magic third hit; level 6 is his stage, not the moment Nasus is cleared to fight. The two layers give opposite instructions for the same moment.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten to dive-survival only. phases[6].side set to Nasus to match its own why and content win[6].

audit.why: suspectNames flagged "Spirit Fire's" in early. False positive — Spirit Fire is Nasus's real E name; the flag is the possessive apostrophe. No edit made.

edits.before: E lets you stack safely from range when Jax zones you. Spirit Fire the wave under tower; every stack denied is his only real win condition.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and dodges basic attacks, not abilities — hold Siphoning Strike, keep Spirit Fire on him, stack from range.

edits.after: Fury of the Sands is dive survival here, not a kill button: Grandmaster-at-Arms hands him armour and magic resist for the whole all-in.

edits.before: That is Jax's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Counter Strike eats basic attacks, and your stacked Q is one of them. Hold it.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms gives him bonus armour and magic resist on demand.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is a pure farm standoff — you have no ult and few stacks, so just last-hit with Q and accept some chip; neither of you wants a real fight yet. The danger starts at 3 when Jax has Counter Strike: if you walk up to land a stacked Q auto into his E, he dodges it, stuns you and W-Qs you for free. Throw Q on minions, not on him, and use Spirit Fire's armor-shred zone to farm and stack from range instead of trading.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is a pure farm standoff — you have no ult and few stacks, so just last-hit with Q and accept some chip; neither of you wants a real fight yet. The danger starts at 3 when Jax has Counter Strike: walk up with a stacked Q into his E and he dodges it, stuns you and W-Qs you for free. It is 17s at rank 1, so hold Q for minions and keep Spirit Fire under him — it is an ability, so his E does not dodge it.

edits.before: This is Jax's window, not yours. Levels 4-6 he wants short Q-W-E trades on cooldown, and his first-item Sheen spike chunks you while you still only have stacks. Wither is your only answer — burn it the instant he leaps so his Empower attack speed and E dodge are dead, then walk away; do not try to win the extended fight yet. At 6 respect that his R bonus armor/MR and magic third-hit make him tankier than you in a straight all-in, so ult only to survive a committed dive, not to chase a kill.
edits.after: This is Jax's window, not yours. Levels 4-6 he wants short Leap Strike-Empower-Counter Strike trades on cooldown, and his first-item Sheen spike chunks you while you still only have stacks. Wither is your only answer — burn it the instant he leaps, so Relentless Assault and his E's dodge value both die, then walk away. At 6, Grandmaster-at-Arms hands him armour, magic resist and a magic third hit, so ult to survive a dive, never to chase a kill.

edits.before: This is where you take over and never give it back. With enough Q stacks plus ult and Wither, you lock his attack speed to zero — his entire E-dodge-and-Empower kit relies on auto-attacking, so a Withered Jax does almost nothing while your stacked Q one-shots him through his R. Force the splitpush 1v1: he can leap to you, but he can't out-duel a fully stacked Nasus who slows his autos and out-sustains the fight. Just survive to items and the lane is yours.
edits.after: This is where you take over and never give it back. With enough Q stacks plus ult and Wither, you lock his attack speed to zero — Relentless Assault, Counter Strike's dodge and Grandmaster-at-Arms' third hit all need him swinging, so a Withered Jax does almost nothing while your stacked Q one-shots him through his R. Force the splitpush 1v1: he can leap to you, but he can't out-duel a fully stacked Nasus. Survive to items and the lane is yours.

edits.after: Now your stacked Q plus ult plus Wither shut off Relentless Assault and Counter Strike's dodge value — you reclaim the lane for good.

edits.after: Jax gets Counter Strike (E) — 17s at rank 1 and it dodges basic attacks only, so never throw an empowered Q into that window.

notes: champ-data/_kits/jax.json carries a 'dash' flag on Empower (W). Empower is a bonus-damage auto reset with no movement component — that flag looks like a derivation artifact from the wording 'charges his weapon', and nothing here was written from it. Worth checking whether the same false dash flag has propagated into other Jax matchups. Separately: I did not touch the level chart despite the flagged contradiction, because Jax really does own levels 2 through first item and inventing a Nasus stage there would be dangerous advice; the difficulty label was the actual error and that is what I corrected.
